sanskrit: idam itthā raudraṃ gūrtavacā brahma kratvā śacyām antar ājau | krāṇā yad asya pitarā maṃhaneṣṭhāḥ parṣat pakthe ahann ā sapta hotṝn ||
english: This praise-hymn truly Rudraic, rich in laud, was found through insight and power in the midst of battle; when his parents, most bountiful, were creating, may he lead the group, may he smite and summon the seven priests.

sanskrit: sa id dānāya dabhyāya vanvañ cyavānaḥ sūdair amimīta vedim | tūrvayāṇo gūrtavacastamaḥ kṣodo na reta itaūti siñcat ||
english: He, striving to win a gift worthy of gratitude — Cyavana — measured out the altar with skilled hands; he the foremost in sweet speech, pressing ever onward, poured forth semen as a flood of water flowing.

sanskrit: mano na yeṣu havaneṣu tigmaṃ vipaḥ śacyā vanutho dravantā | ā yaḥ śaryābhis tuvinṛmṇo asyāśrīṇītādiśaṃ gabhastau ||
english: Like the mind, sharp in those invocations — you two inspired ones, swiftly moving, win by your power; he who, mighty in strength, with his shafts laid blood upon his arm's direction and smote it.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇā yad goṣv aruṇīṣu sīdad divo napātāśvinā huve vām | vītam me yajñam ā gatam me annaṃ vavanvāṃsā neṣam asmṛtadhrū ||
english: When the dark one settled among the ruddy cows, I call upon you, O Aśvins, grandsons of Heaven; come to my sacrifice, come to my food, you who have won your way, guiding without forgetfulness.

sanskrit: prathistha yasya vīrakarmamiṣṇad anuṣṭhitaṃ nu naryo apauhat | punas tad ā vṛhati yat kanāyā duhitur ā anubhṛtam anarvā ||
english: He whose heroic deed was set in motion and accomplished — the manly one thrust it away; he draws back again what was carried away from the maiden, borne along from his daughter, he the unhurt one.

sanskrit: madhyā yat kartvam abhavad abhīke kāmaṃ kṛṇvāne pitari yuvatyām | manānag reto jahatur viyantā sānau niṣiktaṃ sukṛtasya yonau ||
english: When in the midst there arose what had to be done in the encounter — the father making love to the young woman — the two, parting asunder, let fall a little seed; it was poured upon the back, in the womb of the one who had done well.

sanskrit: pitā yat svāṃ duhitaram adhiṣkan kṣmayā retaḥ saṃjagmāno ni ṣiñcat | svādhyo 'janayan brahma devā vāstoṣ patiṃ vratapāṃ nir atakṣan ||
english: When the father, mounting his own daughter, united with her on the ground and poured forth his seed — the gods, deep in thought, generated the sacred hymn and fashioned Vāstoṣpati, the guardian of vows.

sanskrit: sa īṃ vṛṣā na phenam asyad ājau smad ā paraidd apa dabhraceṭāḥ | sarat padā na dakṣiṇā parāvṛṅ na tā nu me pṛśanyo jagṛbhre ||
english: He, like a bull, shot forth foam in the contest; he who was poor in wisdom went away from there; the right hand turned back running like a foot — those speckled ones did not seize them for me.

sanskrit: makṣū na vahniḥ prajāyā upabdir agniṃ na nagnaḥ upa sīdad ūdhaḥ | sanitedhmam sanitota vājaṃ sa dhartā jajñe sahasā yavīyut ||
english: Like a swift carrier eagerly approaching the offspring, like a naked one approaching the udder of fire; he who wins the fuel and wins also the prize — that supporter was born with force, ever youthful.

sanskrit: makṣū kanāyāḥ sakhyaṃ navagvā ṛtaṃ vadanta ṛtayuktim agman | dvibarhasaḥ ya upa gopam āgur adakṣiṇāso acyutā dudukṣan ||
english: Quickly the Navagvas came to friendship with the maiden, speaking truth and reaching the right season; those of double strength who came to the herdsman — without the right fee — sought to milk the unyielding one.

sanskrit: makṣū kanāyāḥ sakhyaṃ navīyo rādho na reta ṛtam it turanyan | śuci yat te rekṇa āyajanta sabardughāyāḥ paya usriyāyāḥ ||
english: The yet newer friendship of the maiden, like a gift and like seed, hastening toward truth; when they sacrificed to your pure treasure — to the milk of the cow that gives all fullness.

sanskrit: paśvā yat paścā viyutā budhanteti bravīti vaktarī rarāṇaḥ | vasor vastvaṃ kāravo 'nehā viśvaṃ viveṣṭi draviṇam upa kṣu ||
english: When the cattle awaken separated in the rear — so says the speaker, he who is generous — the craftsmen, faultless, seek the substance of riches and pervade all wealth close by.

sanskrit: tad in nv asya pariṣadvāno agman purū sadanto nārṣadam bibhitsan | vi śuṣṇasya saṃgrathitam anarvā vidat puruprajātasya guhā yat ||
english: Those who sit around came to that very thing — sitting in many places, seeking to overcome Nārṣada; the unhurt one opened what was knotted of Śuṣṇa, finding what lay hidden of the many-fathered one.

sanskrit: bhargo ha nāmota yasya devāḥ svar ṇa ye triṣadasthe niṣeduḥ | agnir ha nāmota jātavedāḥ śrudhī no hotar ṛtasya hotādhruk ||
english: Bhar-gas — 'the Radiance' — so the gods call him; like the sun, those who have taken seat in the triple resting-place; Agni too they call Jātavedas — hear us, O Hotṛ, priest of truth, O priest who never fails.

sanskrit: uta tyā me raudrāv arcimantā nāsatyāv indra gūrtaye yajādhyai | manuṣvad vṛktabarhiṣe rarāṇā mandū hitaprayasā vikṣu yajyū ||
english: And those two Rudraic, radiant ones, the Nāsatyas — O Indra — I wish to worship for gladness; like Manu, generous to the one whose grass is strewn, joyful, with offerings set in place, they are worshipped among the folk.

sanskrit: ayaṃ stuto rājā vandi vedhā apaś ca vipras tarati svasetaḥ | sa kakṣīvantaṃ rejayat so agniṃ nemiṃ na cakram arvato raghudhru ||
english: This king, when praised, is a worshipful creator; the inspired one crosses the waters by his own dam; he made Kakṣīvant tremble, he who is Agni, swift and hurling like the rim of a wheel on a racehorse.

sanskrit: sa dvibandhur vaitaraṇo yaṣṭā sabardhuṃ dhenuṃ asvaṃ duhadhyai | saṃ yan mitrāvaruṇā vṛñja ukthair jyeṣṭhebhir aryamaṇaṃ varūthaiḥ ||
english: He the twice-bound, the Vaitaraṇa, the sacrificer — that the cow of all fullness and the horse may be milked; when he unites with lauds Mitra and Varuṇa, with the highest protections of Aryaman.

sanskrit: tadbandhuḥ sūrir divi te dhiyaṃdhā nābhānediṣṭho rapati pra venan | sā no nābhiḥ paramāsya vā ghāhaṃ tat paścā katithaś cid āsa ||
english: Bound to that, the sage in heaven establishes thought; Nābhānediṣṭha speaks forth, piercing deep — that is our navel, and the highest also; I was that, how many soever times in the past.

sanskrit: iyam me nābhir iha me sadastham ime me devā ayam asmi sarvaḥ | dvijā aha prathamajā ṛtasyedaṃ dhenur aduhat jāyamānā ||
english: This is my navel, here is my seat; these are my gods, I am here entire; twice-born, firstborn of truth — this cow yielded her milk as she came into being.

sanskrit: adhāsu mandro aratir vibhāvāva syati dvivarttanir vaneṣāṭ | ūrdhvā yac chreṇir na śiśur dan makṣū sthiraṃ śevṛdhaṃ sūta mātā ||
english: Then the charming, tireless, far-shining one will flow down; he who turns in two directions, conquering the woods — when the row of teeth rises like a child newly grown, the mother swiftly brings forth the hard, swelling member.

sanskrit: adhā gāva upamātiṃ kanāyā anu śvāntasya kasya cit pareyuḥ | śrudi tvaṃ sudrāviṇo nas tvaṃ yāḻ āśvaghnasya vāvṛdhe sūnṛtābhiḥ ||
english: Then the cows followed the likeness of the maiden after someone who had fallen asleep; hear us, you of good treasure — you who have grown by the swift gifts of him who slays horses.

sanskrit: adha tvam indra viddhyasmān maho rāye nṛpate vajrabāhuḥ | rakṣā ca no maghonaḥ pāhi sūrīn anehasas te harivo abhiṣṭau ||
english: Now do you, O Indra, know us, O lord of men, thunderbolt-armed, for great wealth; protect us and guard our liberal lords in your faultless, golden assistance.

sanskrit: adha yad rājānā gaviṣṭau sarat saranyuḥ kārave jaranyuḥ | vipraḥ preṣṭhaḥ sa hy eṣāmm babhuva parā ca vakṣad uta parṣad enān ||
english: And when the two kings in the contest for cattle — Saraṇyu swift-moving and Jaranya toward the singer — the most inspired was dearest among them; he will carry them forward and lead them across.

sanskrit: adhā nv asya jenyasya puṣṭau vṛthā rebhanta īmahe tad ū nu | saraṇyur asya sūnur aśvo vipraś cāsi śravasaś ca sātau ||
english: Now indeed in the prosperity of his conquering wealth we praise freely — that we seek even now; Saraṇyu's son, the horse, and the inspired one are both fighters for fame.

sanskrit: yuvor yadi sakhyāyāsme śardhāya stomaṃ jujuṣe namasvān | viśvatra yasmin ā giraḥ samīcīḥ pūrvīva gātur dāśat sūnṛtāyai ||
english: If for your two's friendship — for our band of heroes — the reverential praise-hymn has found favor; in whom from all sides the converging songs unite, may the path, ancient as ever, be given for truth's song.

sanskrit: sa gṛṇāno adbhir devavān iti subhandhur namasā sūktaiḥ | vardhad ukthair vacobhir ā hi nūnaṃ vy adhvaiti payasa usriyāyāḥ ||
english: He, praised with waters, is truly god-possessed; of good alliance, with reverence and well-spoken hymns, he grows with lauds and words — for now indeed he travels along the milk-stream of the dawn cow.

sanskrit: ta ū ṣu ṇo maho yajatrā bhūta devāsa ūtaye sajoṣāḥ | ye vājām̐ anayatā viyanto ye sthā nicetāro amūrāḥ ||
english: Be you then, O great adorable gods, of one accord for our aid; you who lead prizes hither from afar, you who are the wise, clear-sighted discerners.

sanskrit: ye yajñena dakṣiṇayā samaktā indrasya sakhyam amṛtatvam ānaśa | tebhyo bhadram aṅgiraso vo astu prati gṛbhṇīta māṇavaṃ sumedhasaḥ ||
english: Those who, consecrated by sacrifice and the sacrificial gift, won the friendship of Indra and immortality — to them, O Āṅgirasas, may good fortune come; O wise ones, receive the gift of Manu.

sanskrit: ya udājan pitaro gomayaṃ vasv ṛtenābhindan parivatSare valam | dīrghāyutvam aṅgiraso vo astu prati gṛbhṇīta māṇavaṃ sumedhasaḥ ||
english: Those fathers who drove forth the cow-rich treasure, who with truth broke open the Vala cave in the circling year — long life be yours, O Āṅgirasas; O wise ones, receive the gift of Manu.

sanskrit: ya ṛtena sūryam ārohayandivy aprathayan pṛthivīṃ mātaraṃ vi | suprajāstvam aṅgiraso vo astu prati gṛbhṇīta māṇavaṃ sumedhasaḥ ||
english: Those who by truth raised the sun up into heaven, who spread wide the earth, the mother — good offspring be yours, O Āṅgirasas; O wise ones, receive the gift of Manu.

sanskrit: ayaṃ nābhā vadati valgu vo gṛhe devapuṭrā ṛṣayas tac chṛṇotana | subrahmaṇyam aṅgiraso vo astu prati gṛbhṇīta māṇavaṃ sumedhasaḥ ||
english: This navel-born one speaks sweetly in your home — O sons of gods, O seers, hear this; excellent Brahmanhood be yours, O Āṅgirasas; O wise ones, receive the gift of Manu.

sanskrit: virūpāsa id ṛṣayas ta id gambhīravepasaḥ | te aṅgirasaḥ sūnavas te agneḥ pari jajñire ||
english: Of varied forms are these seers, of deep inspiration — the Āṅgirasas who are his sons were born from Agni himself.

sanskrit: ye agneḥ pari jajñire virūpāso divas pari | navagvo nu daśagvo aṅgirastamas sacā deveṣu maṃhate ||
english: Those who were born around Agni, of varied forms born from Heaven — Navagva and Daśagva, most Āṅgirasa, together are generous among the gods.

sanskrit: indreṇa yujā niḥ sṛjanta vāghato vrajaṃ gomantam aśvinam | sahasram me dadato aṣṭakarṇyāḥ śravo deveṣv akrata ||
english: With Indra as their ally, the inspired singers drove out the cow-and-horse-full pen; the eight-eared ones who gave me a thousand made glory among the gods.

sanskrit: pra nūnaṃ jāyatām ayam manus tokmevā rohatu | yaḥ sahasraṃ śatāśvaṃ sadyo dānāya maṃhate ||
english: Let this Manu now spring forth and grow like a sprouting shoot — he who straightway is generous with a thousand and a hundred horses for the gift.

sanskrit: na tam aśnoti kaś cana diva iva sānv ārabham | sāvarṇyasya dakṣiṇā vi sindhur iva paprathe ||
english: No one reaches it — like the ridge of heaven, untouchable; the bounty of Sāvarṇi has spread wide like a river.

sanskrit: uta dāsā parivise smaddiṣṭī goparīṇasā | yadus turvaś ca māmahe ||
english: And the Dāsas who dwell around, well-directed and girt with cattle — Yadu and Turvaśa too have honored me.

sanskrit: sahasradā grāmaṇīr mā riṣan manus sūryeṇāsya yatamānaitu dakṣiṇā | sāvarṇer devāḥ pra tirantv āyur yasmin aśrāntā asanāma vājam ||
english: The village leader who gives thousands — may Manu not be harmed; may his bounty come forth along with the sun; may the gods extend the life of Sāvarṇi in whom, untired, we shall win the prize.

sanskrit: parāvato ye didiṣanta āpyaṃ manuprītāso janima vivasvaraḥ | yayāter ye nahuṣyasya barhiṣi devā āsate te adhi bruvantu naḥ ||
english: Those gods who shine forth from the distance, kin to the waters, dear to Manu, of Vivasvat's lineage, who sit upon the sacrificial grass of Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa — may they speak on our behalf.

sanskrit: viśvā hi vo namasyāni vandyā nāmāni devā uta yajñiyāni vaḥ | ye stha jātā aditer adbhyas pari ye pṛthivyās te ma iha śrutā havam ||
english: All your names, O gods, are worthy of reverence and praise, and worthy of sacrifice; those of you born from Aditi, from the waters, from the earth — may they hear my call here.

sanskrit: yebhyo mātā madhumat pinvate payaḥ pīyūṣaṃ dyaur aditir adribarhāḥ | ukthaśuṣmān vṛṣabharān svapnasas tām̐ ādityām̐ anu madā svastaye ||
english: Those for whom the mother pours sweet milk as first-flow — Aditi, the heaven, she whose lap is the rock; those mighty with hymns, bull-strong, sleep-bringing Ādityas — rejoice with them for our well-being.

sanskrit: nṛcakṣaso animiṣanto arhaṇā bṛhad devāso amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ | jyotīrathā ahimāyā anāgaso divo varṣmāṇaṃ vasate svastaye ||
english: They watch over men, they are unwinking, worthy of honor; the great gods have attained immortality; their chariots are of light, their magic conquers winter, sinless — they dwell on heaven's height for our well-being.

sanskrit: samrājo ye suvṛdho yajñam āyayur aparihvṛtā dadhire divi kṣayam | tām̐ ā vivāsa namasā suvṛktibhir maho ādityām̐ aditiṃ svastaye ||
english: The universal rulers who grow well, who have come to the sacrifice, who unconfounded have their dwelling in heaven — revere them with reverence and excellent lauds, the great Ādityas and Aditi, for our well-being.

sanskrit: ko vaḥ stomaṃ rādhati yaṃ jujoṣatha viśve devāso manuṣo yati ṣṭhana | ko vo 'dhvaraṃ tuvijātā araṃ karad yo naḥ parṣad aty aṃhaḥ svastaye ||
english: Who among you fulfills the praise that you delight in, O All Gods, wherever you stand among men? Who makes the sacrifice ready for you, mighty-born, who will lead us beyond danger for our well-being?

sanskrit: yebhyo hotrām prathamām āyeje manuḥ samiddhāgnir manasā sapta hotṛbhiḥ | ta ādityā abhayaṃ śarma yacchata sugā naḥ karta supathā svastaye ||
english: Those to whom Manu first offered the priestly call, with kindled fire, in mind, with the seven priests — may those Ādityas grant fearless shelter; make easy our paths, the paths of well-being.

sanskrit: ya īśire bhuvanasya pracetaso viśvasya sthātur jagataś ca mantavaḥ | te naḥ kṛtād akṛtād enasos pary adyā devāsaḥ pipṛtā svastaye ||
english: Those who are lords of the world, the wise, the thinkers of all that is fixed and all that moves — may those gods save us today from guilt done and undone, for our well-being.

sanskrit: bhareṣv indraṃ suhavaṃ havāmahe 'ṃhomucaṃ sukṛtaṃ daivyaṃ janam | agnim mitraṃ varuṇaṃ sātaye bhagaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī marutaḥ svastaye ||
english: In battles we call upon Indra, easy to invoke, the deliverer from distress, doer of good, the divine person; Agni, Mitra, Varuṇa for winning, Bhaga, Heaven and Earth, the Maruts — for our well-being.

sanskrit: sutrāmāṇaṃ pṛthivīṃ dyām anehasaṃ suśarmāṇam aditiṃ supraṇītim | daivīṃ nāvaṃ svaritrām anāgasam asravantīm ā ruhemā svastaye ||
english: Let us mount the good-shielding earth, faultless heaven, Aditi the good-sheltering, good-leading divine ship with good oars, sinless and never sinking, for our well-being.

sanskrit: viśve yajatrā adhi vocatotāye trāyadhvaṃ no durevāyā abhihrutaḥ | satyayā vo devahūtyā huvema śṛṇvato devā avase svastaye ||
english: O all adorable ones, speak out for our aid; protect us from the ill-road and from what assaults us; with your true invocation of gods we call you — O gods who hear, come to our protection and well-being.

sanskrit: apāmīvām apa viśvām anāhutim apārātiṃ durvidatrām aghāyataḥ | āre devā dveṣo asmad yuyotano ru ṇaḥ śarma yacchatā svastaye ||
english: Drive away disease, all evil, the unoffered, ill-will, the hard-to-understand, of the malicious one; O gods, keep enmity far from us; grant us wide shelter for our well-being.

sanskrit: ariṣṭaḥ sa marto viśva edhate pra prajābhir jāyate dharmanas pari | yam ādityāso nayathā sunītibhir ati viśvāni duritā svastaye ||
english: Unharmed, that mortal thrives in everything and multiplies with offspring beyond law; he whom the Ādityas lead with good guidance past all evils — for well-being.

sanskrit: yaṃ devāso 'vatha vājasātau yaṃ śūrasātā maruto hite dhane | prātaryāvāṇaṃ ratham indra sānasim ariṣyantam ā ruhemā svastaye ||
english: He whom the gods protect in the winning of the prize, whom the Maruts, slayers of heroes, protect when prizes are set — on that chariot, going forth at dawn, O Indra, ever victorious, never harmed, let us mount — for well-being.

sanskrit: svasti naḥ pathyāsu dhanvasu svasty apsu vṛjane svarvati | svasti naḥ puṭrakṛtheṣu yoniṣu svasti rāye maruto dadhātana ||
english: Blessing on our roads and on the desert ways, blessing in the waters, in the fortified sun-filled place; blessing on us in the births of sons, in the womb — Maruts, grant us blessing and wealth.

sanskrit: svastir id dhi praprathe śreṣṭhā rekṇasvaty abhi yā vāmam eti | sā no amā so araṇe ni pātu svāveśā bhavatu devagopā ||
english: Blessing, indeed the best as she travels onward, she who brings treasure-wealth, who moves toward the good — may she protect us at home and abroad; may she be the self-entering one, guarded by the gods.

sanskrit: evā plāteḥ sūnur avīvṛdhad vo viśva ādityā adite manīṣī | īśānāso naro amartye nāstāvi jano divyo gayena ||
english: Thus the son of Plāti, the thoughtful one, has magnified you all, O Ādityas, O Aditi; you lordly men — the divine race has been praised by the immortal with his song.

sanskrit: kathā devānāṃ katamasya yāmani sumantu nāma śṛṇvatām manāmahe | ko mṛḻāti katamo no mayas karat katama ūtī abhy ā vavartati ||
english: In the procession of which of the gods shall we think of a welcome name among those who hear? Who will be merciful? Which one will bring us joy? Which one will return to us with his aid?

sanskrit: kratūyanti kratavo hṛtsu dhītayo venanti venāḥ patayantya diśaḥ | na marḍitā vidyate anya ebhyo deveṣu me adhi kāmā ayaṃsata ||
english: The purposes stir the purposes, the thoughts in the hearts; the longing ones desire and fly in all directions — no mercifulness is found other than in these; on the gods my desires have been set.

sanskrit: narā vā śaṃsam pūṣaṇam agohyam agniṃ deveddhame abhy arcase girā | sūryāmāsā candramasā yamaṃ divi tritaṃ vātam uṣasam aktum aśvinā ||
english: With song I honor manly Pūṣan, the unhideable, Agni kindled by the gods; Sūrya and Māsa, the Moon, Yama in heaven, Trita, Vāyu, Uṣas, Aktu, and the Aśvins.

sanskrit: kathā kavis tuvīravān kayā girā bṛhaspatirvāvṛdhate suvṛktibhiḥ | aja ekapāt suhavebhir ṛkvabhir ahiḥ śṛṇotu budhnyo3 havīmani ||
english: How does the seer, mighty in strength, with what song, with excellent praises magnify Bṛhaspati? May Aja Ekapāda, with those whose calls are good and whose hymns are apt, and Ahir Budhnya hear the oblation.

sanskrit: dakṣasya vāditer janmani vrate rājānā mitrāvaruṇā vivāsasi | atūrtapanthāḥ pururatho aryamā saptahotā viṣurūpeṣu janmasu ||
english: In the law of the birth of Dakṣa and Aditi, you seek to favor the two kings Mitra and Varuṇa; Aryaman of unblocked paths and many chariots — the seven-priest, of varied forms in the births.

sanskrit: te no arvantohavanāśruto havaṃ viśve śṛṇvantu vājino mitadravāḥ | sahasrasā medhasātāv iva tmanā maho ye dhanaṃ samitheṣu jabhrireaḥ ||
english: May those swift, contest-hearing ones, all the prize-bearing, carefully moving ones, hear our call; they who by themselves, like a thousand-winning sacrifice, carry off great wealth in the battles.

sanskrit: pra vo vāyuṃ rathayujam puraṃdhiṃ stomai kṛṇudhvaṃ sakhyāya pūṣaṇam | te hi devasya savituḥ savīmani kratuṃ sacante sacitaḥ sacetasaḥ ||
english: Magnify with praises Vāyu, who yokes his chariot, and Pūraṃdhi, seek the friendship of Pūṣan; for they accompany the will of the divine Savitṛ in his impulse, companions together, of one mind.

sanskrit: triḥ sapta sasrā nadyo mahīr apo vanapatīn parvatām̐ agnim ūtaye | kṛśānum astṝn tiṣyaṃ sadhastha ā rudraṃ rudreṣu rudriyaṃ havāmahe ||
english: The thrice-seven rivers, the great waters, for our aid; the forest lords, the mountains, Agni — we call; Kṛśānu, the archers, Tiṣya in his seat, Rudra among the Rudras, the Rudraic one, we invoke.

sanskrit: sarasvatī sarayuḥ sindhur ūrmibhir maho mahīr avasā yantu vakṣaṇīḥ | devīr āpo mātaraḥ sūdayitnvo ghṛtavat payo madhumannno arcata ||
english: May Sarasvatī, Sarayū, and Sindhu with their waves — the great ones, the nourishing rivers — come with aid; O divine waters, O mothers who give good pleasure, sing to us your milk rich as ghee and sweet as honey.

sanskrit: uta mātā bṛhadivā śṛṇotu nas tvaṣṭā devebhir janibhiḥ pitā vacaḥ | ṛbhukṣā vājo rathaspatirbhago raṇvaḥ śaṃsaḥ śaśamānasya pātu naḥ ||
english: May the mother Bṛhadivā hear us, and Tvaṣṭṛ as father with the gods and the birth-goddesses; Ṛbhukṣan, Vāja, Rathaspati, Bhaga, the joyful hymn — may the praise of the self-offering one protect us.

sanskrit: raṇvaḥ saṃdṛṣṭau pitumām̐ iva kṣayo bhadrā rudrāṇāṃ marutām upastutiḥ | gobhiḥ ṣyāma yaśaso janeṣv ā sadā devāsa iḻayā sacemahi ||
english: The sight of him is joyful, like a nourishing dwelling; blessed is the praise-song of Rudrāṇī and the Maruts; may we be renowned with cattle among the folk, always, O gods, let us be joined with refreshment.

sanskrit: yāṃ me dhiyam maruta indra devā adadāta varuṇa mitra yūyam | tāṃ pīpayata payaseva dhenuṃ kuvid giro adhi rathe vahātha ||
english: The vision that you, O Maruts, O Indra, O gods, O Varuṇa, O Mitra — that you have given me: nourish it like a cow with milk; will you indeed carry my songs upon your chariot?

sanskrit: kuvid aṅga prati yathā cid asya naḥ sajātyasya maruto bubodhatha | nābhā yatra prathamaṃ saṃnasāmahe tatra jāmitvam aditir dadhātu naḥ ||
english: Will you, O Maruts, again somehow become aware of this our same-born kinship? There where we first meet at the navel-point — there may Aditi establish our bond of brotherhood.

sanskrit: te hi dyāvāpṛthivī mātarā mahī devī devāñ janmanā yajñiye itaḥ | ubhe bibhṛta ubhayaṃ bharīmabhiḥ purū retāṃsi pitṛbhiś ca siñcataḥ ||
english: For they — the two great mothers Heaven and Earth, the divine goddesses, worshipped by the gods from the beginning — both bear both, with their wealth-bearing ones; they pour manifold seed along with the fathers.

sanskrit: vi ṣā hotrā viśvam aśnoti vāryaṃ bṛhaspatirar amatiḥ panīyasī | grāvā yatra madhuṣud ucyate bṛhad avīvaśanta matibhir manīṣiṇaḥ ||
english: That priestly office spreads and wins all desirable things; Bṛhaspati and Aramatī, the more wonderful; where the pressing stone is called the great honey-presser, the wise men have rejoiced with their thoughts.

sanskrit: evā kavis tuvīravāṃ ṛtajñā draviṇasyur draviṇasaś cakānaḥ | ukthebhir atra matibhiś ca vipro 'pīpayad gayo divyāni janma ||
english: Thus the seer, mighty in strength, knower of truth, seeking wealth, desiring riches — with his lauds and thoughts here the inspired one nourished the heavenly birth of the homestead.

sanskrit: evā plāteḥ sūnur avīvṛdhad vo viśva ādityā adite manīṣī | īśānāso naro amartye nāstāvi jano divyo gayena ||
english: Thus the son of Plāti, the thoughtful one, has magnified you all, O Ādityas, O Aditi; you lordly men — the divine race has been praised by the immortal with his song.

sanskrit: agnir indro varuṇo mitro aryamā vāyuḥ pūṣā sarasvatī sajoṣasaḥ | ādityā viṣṇur marutaḥ svar bṛhat somo rudro aditir brahmaṇas patiḥ ||
english: Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Vāyu, Pūṣan, Sarasvatī — of one accord; the Ādityas, Viṣṇu, the Maruts, the great sun, Soma, Rudra, Aditi, and Brahmaṇaspati.

sanskrit: indrāgnī vṛtrahatyeṣu satpatī mitho hinvānā tanvā samokasā | antariksaṃ mahy ā paprur ojasā somo ghṛtaśrīr mahimānam īrayan ||
english: Indra and Agni, lords of the good in the slaying of Vṛtra, mutually impelling each other, dwelling in the same abode; they filled great mid-air with their might; Soma, gleaming with ghee, stirring forth greatness.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ hi mahnā mahatām anarvaṇāṃ stomām̐ iyarmy ṛtajñā ṛtāvṛdhām | ye apsavam arṇavaṃ citraradhases te no rāsantām mahaye sumitrāḥ ||
english: By the greatness of those great and unhurt ones, knowers of truth, who increase the truth, I urge forth these praises; they who have the streaming wave and marvellous bounty — may they, good allies, grant us greatness.

sanskrit: svarṇaram antariksāṇi rocanā dyāvābhūmī pṛthivīṃ skambhor ojasā | pṛkṣā iva mahayantaḥ surātayo devāḥ stavante manuṣāya sūraya ||
english: Heaven-bright, the mid-spaces, the shining realms, the Heaven and Earth — they prop up the earth with their might; like the nourishing ones, magnifying, of good gifts, the gods, the sages, are praised for Manu.

sanskrit: mitrāya śikṣa varuṇāya dāśuṣe yā samrājā manasā na prayucchaṭaḥ | yayor dhāma dharmaṇā rocate bṛhad yayor ubhe rodasī nādhasī vṛtau ||
english: Seek to please Mitra and give to Varuṇa — those two universal kings who do not fail in mind; whose great abode shines by law, of both of whom both world-halves are encompassed, never lowly.

sanskrit: yā gaur vartanim paryeti niṣkṛtam payo duhānā vratanīr avāratāḥ | sā prabruvāṇā varuṇāya dāśuṣe devebhyo dāśad dhaviṣā vivasvaṭe ||
english: The cow who circles the prepared track, giving milk, obedient to her vow, never failing — she who speaks out, shall give to the one who gives to Varuṇa, shall give to the gods with the offering, to Vivasvat.

sanskrit: divakṣaso agnijihvā ṛtāvṛdha ṛtasya yoniṃ vimṛśanta āsate | dyāṃ skabhitvy apa ā cakrur ojasā yajñaṃ janitvī tanvī ni māmṛjuḥ ||
english: Those who dwell in heaven, whose tongue is fire, who increase truth, who sit contemplating the womb of truth; having propped up the sky they created the waters with might, and having generated the sacrifice they wiped themselves clean.

sanskrit: parikṣitā pitarā pūrvajāvarī ṛtasya yonā kṣayataḥ samokasā | dyāvāpṛthivī varuṇāya savrate ghṛtavat payo mahiṣāya pinvataḥ ||
english: The two parents who guard on every side, the ancient and primeval ones, dwelling together in the womb of truth — Heaven and Earth, sharing the vow of Varuṇa, swell out ghee-rich milk for the great bull.

sanskrit: parjanyāvātā vṛṣabhā purīṣiṇendravāyū varuṇo mitro aryamā | devām̐ ādityām̐ aditiṃ havāmahe ye pārthivāso divyāso apsu ye ||
english: Parjanya and Vāta, the two bulls full of rain; Indra and Vāyu, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman — we call the gods, the Ādityas, and Aditi; those of the earth, those of heaven, those in the waters.

sanskrit: tvaṣṭāraṃ vāyum ṛbhavo ya ohate daivyā hotārā uṣasaṃ svastaye | bṛhaspatiṃ vṛtrakhādaṃ sumedhasam indriyaṃ somaṃ dhanasā u īmahe ||
english: Tvaṣṭṛ, Vāyu, the Ṛbhus who make glad, the two divine priests, Uṣas — for our well-being; Bṛhaspati, who devours Vṛtra, the wise one; Soma, Indra's own — these too we seek as prize-winners.

sanskrit: brahma gām aśvaṃ janayanta oṣadhīr vanapatīn pṛthivīm parvatām̐ apaḥ | sūryaṃ divi rohayantaḥ sudānava āryā vratā visṛjanto adhi kṣami ||
english: They generated the Brahman, the cow, the horse, the herbs, the forest trees, the earth, the mountains, the waters; raising the sun in heaven, the good-giving ones, releasing the noble vows upon the earth.

sanskrit: bhujyum aṃhasaḥ pipṛtho nir aśvinā śyāvam putraṃ vadrimatyā ajinvatam | kamadyuvaṃ vimadāyohathur yuvaṃ viṣṇāpvam̐ viśvakāyāva sṛjathaḥ ||
english: You freed Bhujyu from distress, O Aśvins; you quickened the dark son of Vadhrimatī; you brought a bride to Vimada, the love-passionate one; you two released Viṣṇāpva, the all-bodied.

sanskrit: pāvīravī tanyatur ekapād ajo divo dhartā sindhur āpaḥ samudryaḥ | viśve devāsaḥ śṛṇavan vacāṃsi me sarasvatī saha dhībhiḥ puraṃdhyā ||
english: Pāvīravī, the thunder, one-footed Aja, the support of heaven, Sindhu, the waters, those of the sea — may all the gods hear my words, and Sarasvatī together with her thoughts, the full-gifted one.

sanskrit: viśve devāḥ saha dhībhiḥ puraṃdhyā manor yajatrā amṛtā ṛtajñāḥ | rātiṣāco abhiṣācaḥ svarvidaḥ svar giro brahma sūktaṃ juṣerata ||
english: All the gods, with full thoughts and full gifts, Manu's adorable ones, immortal, knowers of truth; the ones who grant, who approach, who know the sun's realm — may they delight in the solar songs, in the Brahman, in the well-spoken hymn.

sanskrit: devān vasiṣṭho amṛtān vavande ye viśvā bhuvanābhi pratasthuḥ | te no rāsantām urugāyam adya yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: Vasiṣṭha has praised the immortal gods who have spread over all the worlds; may they grant us today the widely-proclaimed; always protect us with blessings.

sanskrit: devān huve bṛhacchrāvasaḥ svastaye jyotiṣkṛto adhvarasya pracetasaḥ | ye vāvṛdhuḥ prataraṃ viśvavedasa indrajyeṣṭhāso amṛtā ṛtāvṛdhaḥ ||
english: I call upon the gods of great glory for our well-being, makers of light, wise in the sacrifice; those who have grown exceedingly, all-knowing, with Indra as their chief, immortal, who increase the truth.

sanskrit: indraprasūtā varuṇapraśiṣṭā ye sūryasya jyotiṣo bhāgam ānaśuḥ | marudgaṇe vṛjane manma dhīmahi māghone yajñaṃ janayanta sūraya ||
english: Impelled by Indra, guided by Varuṇa, those who have attained a share of the light of the sun — in the company of the Maruts, in the fortified place, let us think devotion; may the sages, not being stingy, generate the sacrifice.

sanskrit: indro vasubhiḥ pari pātu no gayam ādityair no aditiḥ śarma yacchatu | rudro rudrebhir devo mṛḻayāti nas tvaṣṭā no gnābhiḥ suvitāya jinvatu ||
english: May Indra with the Vasus guard our home; may Aditi with the Ādityas grant us shelter; may the divine Rudra with the Rudras be gracious to us; may Tvaṣṭṛ with the goddesses quicken us to well-being.

sanskrit: aditir dyāvāpṛthivī ṛtam mahad indrāviṣṇū marutaḥ svar bṛhat | devām̐ ādityām̐ avase havāmahe vasūn rudrān savitāraṃ sudaṃsasam ||
english: Aditi, Heaven and Earth, the great truth, Indra and Viṣṇu, the Maruts, the great sun — we call the Ādityan gods for aid, the Vasus, the Rudras, and Savitṛ of wonderful deeds.

sanskrit: sarasvan dhībhir varuṇo dhṛtavrataḥ pūṣā viṣṇur mahimā vāyur aśvinā | brahmakṛto amṛtā viśvavedaso śarma no yaṃsan trivarūtham aṃhasaḥ ||
english: Sarasvan with his thoughts, Varuṇa who holds to his vow, Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, Mahiman, Vāyu, the Aśvins — makers of Brahman, immortal, all-knowing — may they grant us triple-walled shelter from distress.

sanskrit: vṛṣā yajño vṛṣaṇaḥ santu yajñiyā vṛṣaṇo devā vṛṣaṇo haviṣkṛtaḥ | vṛṣaṇā dyāvāpṛthivī ṛtāvarī vṛṣā parjanyo vṛṣaṇo vṛṣastubhaḥ ||
english: Manly be the sacrifice, let the adorable ones be powerful bulls; bull-like are the gods, bull-like the oblation-makers; manly are Heaven and Earth, the guardians of truth; the bull is Parjanya and manly are those who praise the bull.

sanskrit: agnīṣomā vṛṣaṇā vājasātaye purupraśastā vṛṣaṇā upa bruve | yāv ījire vṛṣaṇo devayajyayā tā naḥ śarma trivarūthaṃ vi yaṃsataḥ ||
english: I call upon Agni and Soma, the mighty bulls, much praised, mighty bulls, for the winning of the prize; those two who have been worshipped as bulls by the worship of the gods — may they grant us triple shelter.

sanskrit: dhṛtavratāḥ kṣatriyā yajñaniṣkṛto bṛhadivā adhvarāṇām abhiśriyaḥ | agnihotāra ṛtasāpo adruho 'po asṛjann anu vṛtratūrye ||
english: Firm in their vow, lordly, performing the sacrifice, of great luster, the glory of the rites; fire-offering, winning truth, without treachery — they released the waters at the conquest of Vṛtra.

sanskrit: dyāvāpṛthivī janayann abhi vratāpa oṣadhīr vanināniyajñiyā | antariksaṃ svar ā paprur ūtaye vaśaṃ devāsas tanvī ni māmṛjuḥ ||
english: Heaven and Earth, generating in accord with their vows, water, herbs, the sacrificial forest plants — they filled the mid-air and the sun for aid; the gods wiped themselves clean upon the willing body.

sanskrit: dhartāro diva ṛbhavaḥ suhastā vātāparjanyā mahiṣasya tanyatoḥ | āpa oṣadhīḥ pra tirantu no giro bhago rātir vājino yantu me havam ||
english: The Ṛbhus, supporters of heaven, skilled-handed; Vāta and Parjanya of the great bull's thunder — may the waters and the herbs extend our songs; may Bhaga, Rāti, and the prize-bearers come to my call.

sanskrit: samudraḥ sindhū rajo antariksam aja ekapāt tanayitnur arṇavaḥ | ahir budhnyaḥ śṛṇavad vacāṃsi me viśve devāsa uta sūrayo mama ||
english: Ocean, the rivers, the dust-realm of mid-air; one-footed Aja, the rumbling wave — may Ahir Budhnya hear my words, and all the gods, and my sages.

sanskrit: syāma vo manavo devavītaye prāñcaṃ no yajñam pra ṇayata sādhuyā | ādityā rudrā vasavaḥ sudānava imā brahma śasyamānāni jinvata ||
english: May we be your Manus for the feast of the gods; lead our sacrifice forward on the good path; O Ādityas, Rudras, Vasus, good-giving ones — quicken these Brahman-words as they are being recited.

sanskrit: daivyā hotārā prathamā purohita ṛtasya panthām anv emi sādhuyā | kṣetrasya patim prativesam īmahe viśvān devām̐ amṛtām̐ aprayucchaṭaḥ ||
english: The two divine priests — first among the household priests — I follow the path of truth rightly; I seek the lord of the field, the neighbor-god; all the immortal gods who do not fail.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhāsaḥ pitṛvad vācam akrata devām̐ īḻānā ṛṣivat svastaye | prītā iva jñātayaḥ kāmam etyāsme devāso 'va dhūnutā vasu ||
english: The Vasiṣṭhas have spoken the word like a father, praising the gods like seers for our well-being; coming as desired like pleased kinsmen — O gods, shake down wealth upon us.

sanskrit: devān vasiṣṭho amṛtān vavande ye viśvā bhuvanābhi pratasthuḥ | te no rāsantām urugāyam adya yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: Vasiṣṭha has praised the immortal gods who have spread over all the worlds; may they grant us today the widely-proclaimed; always protect us with blessings.

sanskrit: imāṃ dhiyaṃ saptaśīrṣṇīm pitā na ṛtaprajātāṃ bṛhatīm avindat | turīyam svij janayad viśvajanyo 'yāsya uktham indrāya śaṃsan ||
english: Our father found this vision of seven heads, born from truth, the vast one; truly the universal Ayāsya generated the fourth — reciting the laud for Indra.

sanskrit: ṛtaṃ śaṃsanta ṛju dīdhyānā divas putrāso asurasy vīrāḥ | vipraṃ padam aṅgiraso dadhānā yajñasya dhāma prathamam mananta ||
english: Reciting truth, thinking straight — the sons of heaven, the heroes of Asura; the Āṅgirasas, bearing the inspired seat, thought on the first abode of the sacrifice.

sanskrit: haṃsair iva sakhibhir vāvadadbhir aśmanmayāni nahanā vyasyan | bṛhaspatirabhi kanikradat gā uta prāstaud uc ca vidvāṃ agāyat ||
english: Like swans with chattering companions, loosening the rocky fetters — Bṛhaspati, roaring forth, drove the cows and sent them away; the knowing one sang out loud.

sanskrit: avo dvābhyāṃ para ekayā gā guhā tiṣṭhantīr anṛtasya setau | bṛhaspatis tamasi jyotir icchannn ud usrā ākar vi hi tisra āvaḥ ||
english: Down from two and beyond the third — the cows standing hidden in the bondage of falsehood; Bṛhaspati seeking light in the darkness drove the dawns upward, for he opened all three.

sanskrit: vibhidyā puraṃ śayaṭhem apācīṃ nis trīṇi sākam udadher akṛntat | bṛhaspatiruṣasaṃ sūryaṃ gām arkaṃ viveda stanayann iva dyauḥ ||
english: Splitting apart the eastward-lying city, he cut off three together from the ocean; Bṛhaspati found the Dawn, the Sun, the cow, and the hymn — thundering as the sky.

sanskrit: indro valaṃ rakṣitāraṃ dughānāṃ kareṇeva vi cartā raveṇa | svedāñjibhir āśiram icchamāno 'rodayat paṇim ā gā amuṣṇāt ||
english: Indra split open Vala, the guardian of the milch cows, like an elephant with his roar; seeking the rich mixture with his sweat-smeared limbs, he made the Paṇi weep and seized the cows.

sanskrit: sa īṃ satyebhiḥ sakhibhiḥ śucadbhir godhāyasaṃ vi dhanasair adardaḥ | brahmaṇas patir vṛṣabhir varāhair gharmasvdebhir draviṇaṃ vy ānaṭ ||
english: He, with his true, shining companions, burst asunder the bow-stringed one with prize-seeking; Brahmaṇaspati distributed the wealth with bulls and boars who sweat with heat.

sanskrit: te satyena manasā gopatiṃ gā iyānāsā iṣaṇayanta dhībhiḥ | bṛhaspatiś ca mithoavadyapebhir ud usriyā asṛjata svayugbhiḥ ||
english: They, with truthful minds, seeking the lord of cattle, set the cows in motion with their thoughts; Bṛhaspati, and those who drink away blame of one another, released the dawn cows with their own yokings.

sanskrit: taṃ vardhayanto matibhiḥ śivābhiḥ siṃham iva nānadataṃ sadhasthe | bṛhaspatiṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ śūrasātau bhare-bhare anu madema jiṣṇum ||
english: Magnifying him with auspicious thoughts — him who roars like a lion in his seat — may we rejoice after Bṛhaspati, the mighty bull, the victorious, in every battle and contest.

sanskrit: yadā vājam asanad viśvarūpaṃ ā dyām arukṣad uttarāṇi sadma | bṛhaspatiṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ vardhayanto nānā santo bibhrato jyotir āsā ||
english: When he won the prize of all forms and climbed to heaven, to the upper dwellings — magnifying Bṛhaspati, the bull, though separated, they bore the light in their mouths.

sanskrit: satyām āśiṣam kṛṇutā vayodhai kīriṃ cid dhy avatha svebhir evaiḥ | paścā mṛdho apa bhavantu viśvās tad rodasī śṛṇutaṃ viśvaminve ||
english: Make true the blessing with your life-giving ones, for you protect even the singer with your own forces; may all the enemies be thrust to the rear — hear this, O Heaven and Earth, you who are all-pervading.

sanskrit: indro mahnā mahato arṇavasya vi mūrdhānam abhinad arbudasya | ahann ahim ariṇāt sapta sindhūn devair dyāvāpṛthivī prāvataṃ naḥ ||
english: Indra with his might shattered the head of great Arbuda of the great wave; he slew the serpent and released the seven rivers — may Heaven and Earth together with the gods protect us.

sanskrit: udapruto na vayo rakṣamāṇā vāvadato abhriyasyeva ghoṣāḥ | giribhrajo normayo madanto bṛhaspatiṃ abhy arka anāvan ||
english: Like birds protecting their watering place, babbling like the sound of a thunder-cloud — the mountain-leaping waves in joy roared forth to Bṛhaspati with their songs.

sanskrit: saṃ gobhir āṅgiraso nakṣamāṇo bhaga ived aryamaṇaṃ nināya | jane mitro na dampatī anakti bṛhaspate vājayāśūm̐r ivājau ||
english: The Āṅgirasa, reaching his goal with the cows, led forth as Bhaga leads Aryaman; like Mitra he anoints the lord and lady among the folk — O Bṛhaspati, urge on the swift ones in the contest.

sanskrit: sādhvaryā ātithinīr iṣirāḥ spārhāḥ suvarṇā anavadyarūpāḥ | bṛhaspatiḥ parvatebhyo vitūryā nir gā ūpe yavam iva sthibhyaḥ ||
english: Going straight, like guests arriving, vigorous, desirable, beautifully golden, of blameless form — Bṛhaspati sifted the cows out from the mountains as if threshing grain from the straw.

sanskrit: āpruṣāyan madhunaḥ ṛtasya yonim avakṣipanṃ arka ulkām iva dyoḥ | bṛhaspatiruddharann aśmano gā bhūmyā udneva vi tvacam bibheda ||
english: Sprinkling the womb of honey and truth, the hymn hurled like a meteor from heaven; Bṛhaspati, lifting the cows from the rock, split the earth's skin as with water.

sanskrit: apa jyotiṣā tamo antariksād udnaḥ śīpālam iva vāta ājat | bṛhaspatiranumṛśyā valasyābhram iva vāta ā cakra ā gāḥ ||
english: With light he drove darkness from the midair as wind drives moss from the water; Bṛhaspati, having stroked the cloud of Vala, brought in the cows like the wind brings a cloud.

sanskrit: yadā valasya pīyato jasum bhed bṛhaspatiragnitapobhir arkaiḥ | dadbhir na jihvā parivṣṭam ādad āvir nidhīm̐r akṛṇod usriyāṇām ||
english: When Bṛhaspati broke the vitality of the abusive Vala with fire-heated hymns — as a tongue laps up what surrounds the teeth — he revealed the hidden stores of the dawn cows.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatiramata hi tyad āsāṃ nāma svarīṇāṃ sadane guhā yat | āṇḍeva bhitvā śakunasya garbham ud usriyāḥ parvatasy tmanājat ||
english: Bṛhaspati knew the hidden name of those sun-cows in their dwelling in the secret place; like breaking the egg of a bird, he drove the dawn cows up from the mountain by himself.

sanskrit: aśnāpinaddham madhu pary apaśyan matsyaṃ na dīna udani kṣiyantam | niṣ taj jabhāra camasaṃ na vṛkṣādbṛhaspatirvireṇā vikṛtya ||
english: He saw honey encased in stone, like a low fish lodged in water; Bṛhaspati tore that out as a cup from a tree, cleaving it with a roar.

sanskrit: soṣām avinda sa svaḥ so agniṃ so arkeṇa vi bābadhe tamāṃsi | bṛhaspatirguvapuṣo valasya nir majjānam na parvaṇo jabhāra ||
english: He found the Uṣases, he found the sun, he found Agni; he pushed back the darkness with the hymn; Bṛhaspati tore out the marrow of Vala who was cow-bodied, as one does from a joint.

sanskrit: himeva parṇā muṣitā vanāni bṛhaspatinākṛpayad valo gāḥ | anānukṛtyam apunaś cakāra yāt sūryāmāsā mitho uccarātaḥ ||
english: As frost strips leaves from forests, Vala wept for his cows taken by Bṛhaspati; what was done could not be undone, done irrevocably — as the sun and moon rise alternating from each other.

sanskrit: abhi śyāvaṃ na kṛśanebhir aśvaṃ nakṣatrebhiḥ pitaro dyām apiṃśan | rātryāṃ tamo adadhur jyotir ahan bṛhaspatirbhinad adriṃ vidad gāḥ ||
english: Like decorating a dark horse with ornamental stones, the fathers decorated heaven with the stars; they set darkness in the night, light in the day — Bṛhaspati clove the rock and found the cows.

sanskrit: idam akarmā namo abhriyāya yaḥ pūrvīr anv ānõnavīti | bṛhaspatiḥ sa hi gobhiḥ so aśvai sa vīrebhiḥ sa nṛbhir no vayo dhāt ||
english: We have done this reverence to him who echoes like a thundercloud, who follows after the many; Bṛhaspati — may he set life-power for us with cattle, with horses, with heroes, with men.

sanskrit: bhadrā agner vādhrya-aśvasya saṃdṛśo vāmī praṇītiḥ suraṇā upetayaḥ | yad īṃ sumitrā viśo agra indhate ghṛtenāhuto jarate davidy-utat ||
english: Blessed is the sight of Agni Vādhrya-aśva, beautiful his leadership, his coming pleasant; when the Sumitras kindle him at the head of the folk, fed with ghee, he shines and blazes forth.

sanskrit: ghṛtam agner vādhrya-aśvasya vardhanam ghṛtam annaṃ ghṛtam v asya medanam | ghṛtenāhuta urviyā vi paprathe sūrya iva rocate sarpirāsutiḥ ||
english: Ghee is the growth of Agni Vādhrya-aśva, ghee is his food, ghee is his nourishment; fed with ghee he spreads out widely — the oblation of clarified butter glows like the sun.

sanskrit: yat te manu yad anīkaṃ sumitraḥ samīdhe agne tad idaṃ navīyaḥ | sa revac choca sa giro juṣasva sa vājaṃ darṣi sa iha śravo dhāḥ ||
english: That face of yours, O Agni, that Manu kindled, that Sumitrā kindled — may this now be newer; shine brilliantly, take delight in the songs, win the prize, and establish glory here.

sanskrit: yaṃ tvā pūrvam īḻito vādhrya-aśvaḥ samīdhe agne sa idaṃ juṣasva | sa naḥ stipā uta bhavā tanūpā dātraṃ rakṣasva yad idaṃ te asme ||
english: That you whom Vādhrya-aśva, the praised one, first kindled, O Agni — may he now take delight in this; be our protector and body-guard; protect the gift that this here is for you from us.

sanskrit: bhavā dyumnī vādhrya-aśvota gopā mā tvā tārīd abhimātir janānām | śūra iva dhṛṣṇuś cyavanaḥ sumitraḥ pra nu vocaṃ vādhrya-aśvasya nāma ||
english: Be glorious and be a herdsman for Vādhrya-aśva; may the ill-will of men not pass beyond you; bold as a hero, moving on, the Sumitrā — now I shall proclaim the name of Vādhrya-aśva.

sanskrit: sam ajryā parvatyā vasūni dāsā vṛtrāṇy āryā jigetha | śūra iva dhṛṣṇuś cyavano janānāṃ tvam agne pṛtanāyūm̐r abhi ṣyāḥ ||
english: You gathered the level and mountain treasures; you conquered the Dāsa hosts and the Ārya foes; bold as a hero, moving men — do you, O Agni, overwhelm those who make battle against us.

sanskrit: dīrghatantur bṛhadukhāyam agniḥ sahasrastarīḥ śatanītha ṛbhvā | dyumān dyumatsu nṛbhir mṛjyamānaḥ sumiṭreṣu dīdayo devayatsu ||
english: Of far-stretching flame, of great udder is this Agni; with a thousand stars, with a hundred paths, skillful; brilliant among the brilliant, tended by men, he shines among the Sumitras who seek the gods.

sanskrit: tve dhenus sudughā jātavedo 'sascateva samanā sabarduk | tvaṃ nṛbhir dakṣiṇāvadbhir agne sumiṭrebhir idhyase devayad-bhiḥ ||
english: In you, O Jātavedas, a well-milking cow pours freely, the inexhaustible, of all fullness; O Agni, you are kindled by men of good gifts, by the Sumitras who seek the gods.

sanskrit: devāś cit te amṛtā jātavedo mahimānaṃ vādhrya-aśva pra vocan | yat sampṛccham mānaṣīr viśa āyan tvaṃ nṛbhir ajayas tvāvṛdhe-bhiḥ ||
english: Even the immortal gods, O Jātavedas, proclaimed the greatness of Vādhrya-aśva; when human folk came to consult you, you conquered with the men who magnified you.

sanskrit: piteva putraṃ abibhar upasthe tvām agne vādhrya-aśvaḥ sapayan | juṣāṇo asya samidam yaviṣṭho uta pūrvām̐ avano vṛādhatāś cit ||
english: Like a father bearing a son upon his lap, Vādhrya-aśva has tended you, O Agni; taking pleasure in his fuel — the youngest one — you overcame those who had grown weak, even the earlier ones.

sanskrit: śaśvad agnir vādhrya-aśvasya śatrūn nṛbhir jigāya sutasomavadbhiḥ | samanaṃ cid adahaś citrabhāno 'va vrādhan-tam abhinad vṛdhaś cit ||
english: Always Agni has overcome the enemies of Vādhrya-aśva with men who press Soma; you burned the common meeting-place, O bright-shining one; you struck down even the growing one who had grown weak.

sanskrit: ayam agnir vādhrya-aśvasya vṛtrahā sanakāt preddho namasopavākyaḥ | sa no ajāmīm̐r uta vā vijāmīn abhi tiṣṭha śardhato vādhrya-aśva ||
english: This Agni of Vādhrya-aśva, the Vṛtra-slayer, kindled of old, to be invoked with reverence — may he stand over our non-kinsmen and kinsmen alike; overwhelm those who are hostile, O Vādhrya-aśva.

sanskrit: imām me agne samidam juṣasve ḻas pade prati haryā ghṛtācīm | varṣman pṛthivyāḥ sudinatve ahnām ūrdhvo bhava sukrato devayajyā ||
english: O Agni, take pleasure in this my fuel at Iḷā's place, delight in the ghee-laden offering; on the heights of the earth, in the clear days, rise up straight for the worship of the gods, O wise one.

sanskrit: ā devānām agrayāve iha yātu narāśaṃso viśvarūpebhir aśvaiḥ | ṛtasya pathā namasā miyedho devebhyo devatamaḥ suṣūdat ||
english: May Narāśaṃsa, first-farer of the gods, come here with his all-formed horses; let the most divine among the divine ones, along the path of truth with reverence, drip the sacrificial offering for the gods.

sanskrit: śaśvat tamam īḻate dūtyāya haviṣmanto manuṣyāso agnim | vahiṣṭhair aśvaiḥ suvṛtā rathena devān vakṣi ni ṣad iha hotā ||
english: Most frequently do those men who hold the oblation beseech Agni for the embassy; with swiftest horses, with well-rolling chariot, bring hither the gods; sit down here as Hotṛ.

sanskrit: vi prathatāṃ devajuṣṭaṃ tirascā dīrghaṃ drāghmā surabhi bhūtv asme | aheḻatā manasā deva barhir indrajyeṣṭhām̐ uśato yakṣi devān ||
english: Let the god-beloved sacred grass be spread out crosswise, long and fragrant for us; with an unhostile mind, O god, worship with the barhis the willing gods with Indra as their chief.

sanskrit: divo vā sānu spṛśatā varīyaḥ pṛthivyā vā mātrayvā vi śrayadhvam | uśatīr dvāro mahinā mahadbhir devaṃ rathaṃ rathayur dhārayadhvam ||
english: Touch the higher ridge of heaven, or spread out with the full measure of the earth; O eager divine doors, with greatness through the great ones, support the divine chariot of the chariot-lover.

sanskrit: devī divo duhitarā suśilpe uṣāsānaktā sadatāṃ ni yonau | ā vāṃ devāsa uśatī uśanta urau sīdantu subhage upasthe ||
english: The two divine daughters of heaven, of beautiful craft — Dawn and Night — let them sit down in their place; may the gods, eager and willing, sit in your wide, blessed lap, O you two.

sanskrit: ūrdhvo grāvā bṛhad agniḥ samiddhaḥ priyā dhāmāny aditer upasthe | purohitāv ṛtvijā yajñe asmin viduṣṭarā draviṇam ā yajethām ||
english: The pressing stone stands upright, the great fire is kindled, in the dear abodes in Aditi's lap; the two household priests, the seasonal sacrificers in this sacrifice — may the more knowing ones gain wealth through worship.

sanskrit: tisro devīr barhir idaṃ varīya ā sīdata cakṛmā vaḥ syonam | manuṣvad yajñaṃ sudhitā havīṃṣī ḷā devī ghṛtapadī juṣanta ||
english: O three goddesses — Iḷā, Sarasvatī, Mahī — take your seat on this best-of-barhis which we have made comfortable; may the divine Iḷā, with ghee-steps, take pleasure in the sacrifice set right as Manu's, with well-placed oblations.

sanskrit: deva tvaṣṭar yad dha cārutvam ānaḍ yad aṅgirasām abhavaḥ sacābhūḥ | sa devānāṃ pātha upa pra vidvāṃ uśan yakṣi draviṇodaḥ suratnaḥ ||
english: O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, when you attained charm, when you became a companion of the Āṅgirasas — knowing that, approach the path of the gods; eager, O giver of wealth, of good treasure, do you worship.

sanskrit: vanaspate raśanayā niyūyā devānāṃ pātha upa vakṣi vidvān | svadāti devaḥ kṛṇavad dhaviṃṣy avatāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī havam me ||
english: O Lord of the Forest, bound with the cord, knowing — bring hither along the path of the gods; may the god make the oblations sweet; may Heaven and Earth protect my call.

sanskrit: āgne vaha varuṇam iṣṭaye na indraṃ divo maruto antariksāt | sīdantu barhir viśva ā yajatrā svāhā devā amṛtā mādayantām ||
english: O Agni, bring Varuṇa for our worship, and Indra from the sky, the Maruts from mid-air; may all the adorable ones take their seat on the barhis — Svāhā! May the immortal gods rejoice.
